title: Programs & Projects Director, xScale (Deal Program Lead)
location_raw: Ashburn; Toronto; Chicago; New York; Dallas Infomart Office DAI; Tampa
description:
Who are we?
Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

About the Role
We are looking for a highly organized, analytical, and proactive Programs & Projects Director to partner to lead execution of large, complex data center deals. In this role, you will act as the central coordination point across Sales, Design & Construction, Legal, and Operations delivery teams—ensuring alignment from early deal qualification through contract signature.

You will thrive in ambiguity, bring structure to complexity, and translate large volumes of information into clear, actionable insights. This is a high-impact role where your ability to influence without authority, anticipate risks, and drive clarity will directly shape business outcomes.

What You’ll Do

Lead Complex Deal Programs

- Serve as Program Lead for coordination and orchestration of strategic xScale deals from qualification through design and contract execution

- Partner with Deal Leads, Account Execs, TPMs, Sales Engineers, Legal, and cross-functional teams to drive program alignment

- Balance customer expectations with operational feasibility to ensure commitments are deliverable

Drive Execution & Coordination

- Improve deal cycle time and contract velocity through disciplined program execution

- Capture detailed notes and produce concise, high-quality executive readouts

- Lead meetings, track actions, and ensure timely follow-through across stakeholders

- Maintain risk, issue, and dependency trackers; proactively drive resolution

Influence & Align Stakeholders

- Act as a bridge between Sales, Legal, Design, Construction, Operations, and Delivery teams, navigating competing priorities

- Facilitate productive conversations and help resolve conflicts across teams

- Build strong relationships across a matrixed organization

Ensure Risk & Compliance Alignment

- Ensure customer commitments align with delivery capability

- Identify and mitigate risks that could impact timelines, cost, or compliance

- Support contract negotiations by managing issue tracking and stakeholder alignment

Drive Continuous Improvement

- Lead or contribute to lessons learned sessions

- Identify and implement improvements to simplify processes and enhance deal execution

What We’re Looking For

Core Skills & Attributes

- Exceptional critical thinking and problem-solving skills

- Highly detail-oriented and methodical, with strong organizational discipline

- Ability to simplify complex information into clear insights and summaries

- Comfortable working independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment

- Strong ability to connect the dots across disparate information sources

Communication & Influence

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills (strong writing backgrounds highly valued)

- Ability to influence cross-functional teams without direct authority

- Proven ability to build trust and navigate complex stakeholder dynamics

Experience

- 10+ years in program management, deal execution, or sales operations

- Experience leading large, cross-functional initiatives

- Familiarity with data center, infrastructure, or related industries preferred

- Sales or commercial operations experience is a plus

Why This Role Matters
You will play a critical role in transforming complex deal environments into aligned, executable programs—helping the organization move faster, make better decisions, and deliver on customer commitments with confidence.

title: Director, Corporate Development
location_raw: Denver; Toronto; Dallas Infomart Office DAI
description:
Who are we?
Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary
The Director, Corporate Development supports Equinix’s AMER investment strategy, partnering cross-functionally on capital sourcing, deal execution and portfolio prioritization. The Director represents Corporate Development in formal presentations to the Investment Committee and senior management on capital structuring, allocation and prioritization decisions. The Director builds a regional view of capital deployment across organic expansion, joint ventures and third-party capital partnerships, ensuring investment recommendations to the Investment Committee are rigorously underwritten and clearly presented. The role demands strong collaboration skills, sound financial modeling and capital markets judgment, and the communication skills to operate credibly in front of senior executives and external capital partners.

Responsibilities
Third-Party Capital Sourcing and Execution

- Leads sourcing and evaluation of third-party capital partners to fund AMER expansion, in partnership with Treasury, Finance and other relevant teams

- Supports structuring and negotiation of commercial terms for capital partnerships and joint ventures, protecting Equinix’s economic and control interests

- Manages execution of capital transactions end-to-end, from initial term sheet through diligence, documentation and closing, in coordination with deal teams

- Builds and maintains a network of capital markets counterparties, institutional investors and joint venture partners active in the data center sector

Capital Allocation and Prioritization

- Contributes to, maintains and recalibrates the AMER capital allocation and prioritization framework as portfolio conditions and capital availability evolve

- Evaluates trade-offs between organic expansion, third-party capital partnerships and portfolio actions to optimize capital efficiency and preserve balance sheet capacity

- Aligns capex budgets and forecasts with portfolio strategy, demand signals and capital availability

- Prepares and presents investment recommendations and capital structures to the Real Estate Investment Committee and other governance bodies

M&A and Strategic Transactions

- Drives origination, negotiation and execution of M&A and strategic transactions in sectors of strategic interest to Equinix, driving cross-team workstreams through to completion

- Evaluates structural alternatives (build versus buy, equity investment versus partnership versus acquisition versus capital partnership) to inform deal structuring recommendations

- Develops the investment and capital partnership thesis and supporting operational models, synergy forecasts and capital structure analysis, in conjunction with Business Unit Heads

- Storyboards presentations to drive discussion at the Senior Executive level and with the Investment Committee

Project and Program Management

- Operates autonomously on multi-month and multi-quarter initiatives, anticipating issues and recommending solutions with limited need for direction from VPs or Country Managers

- Runs interdepartmental project management processes and meetings, coordinating delivery of company-wide and regional strategic programs

- Prepares materials and provides updates for the E-team, senior leadership and Board of Directors

Qualifications

- 10 years of experience in Corporate Finance, Investment Banking, Principal Investing or Corporate Development, with direct experience sourcing or executing third-party capital transactions

- Demonstrated experience preparing and presenting investment recommendations to Investment Committees or equivalent governance bodies

- Data center experience helpful but not required

title: Design Principal, Engineering Development (Mechanical)
location_raw: Redwood City; New York City Office NYO1; Dallas Infomart Office DAI
description:
Who are we?
Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary
The Design Principal is responsible for design decisions related to a portfolio of datacenter projects which can include: new construction, phased expansion, retrofits and upgrades, acquisition conversions, M&E equipment selections, and standards upgrades in either a specific region or globally. They are an exceptional industry professional progressing towards becoming a recognised expert on datacenter design. The Design Principal critically assesses design decisions with consultation with more senior staff across disciplines and applies required Equinix standards and country specific regulations to make the best design choices. They manage the relationship and output of key design partners and equipment suppliers for their assigned projects and critically assess and escalate issues where the relationship with such partners is not meeting expectations.

Responsibilities
The Design Principal, Engineering Development (Mechanical), reporting to the Director, Global Engineering Development, has responsibility for:

- Global mechanical engineering direction of Equinix design through continued development of Equinix’s Reference Designs

- Evaluation of new products and engineering approaches, supporting the Innovation incubation process, for incorporation into the Reference Design on reaching maturity

- Supports Regional Design teams with project implementation of Reference Design

- Provides subject matter expert direction to the Major Capital Equipment (MCE) team dealing with portfolio-wide procurement of mechanical equipment

- Engages with key customers to ascertain their continuously evolving design requirements and directs Reference Design configurations to meet those customer design requirements

Design Process

- Owns and leads a design process, interacting with Architectural, MEP, and other design partners to deliver a portfolio of world class datacenters with a strong focus on technical excellence, mission critical resilience and cost management

- Reviews and contributes to the development of globally standardized tools, techniques and processes for the management and reporting of the design process

- Works with peers in other regions to drive consistency and technical excellence on design and delivery practices and methodologies

- Thinks and acts in a global manner, considering the applicability of any design decision, innovations or standards changes for all regions

- Conducts the master planning of expansion portfolio using global design standards and templates; incorporating regional information to apply these to the inception of projects

- Generates project visualization, initial model using reference design templates and cost estimate for business case inception

- Liaises with regional team to incorporate local infrastructure into the design

- Liaises with commercial management team regionally and globally to assist business case generation

- Liaises with regional team to procure local variations on equipment where Reference Design equipment selections are not available

- Prepares regional-specific and customer-specific configurations of the Reference Design, reacting to local market conditions and customer requirements

Cross-Functional Co-ordination

- Maintains interpersonal relationships with internal technical staff, external design consulting partners, construction management, commercial management, and regional P&L holders to ensure appropriate stakeholder exposure and buy in to Data Center projects

- Appropriately leverages the center of excellence teams and more senior Design staff to augment their individual technical expertise to ensure all facets of the datacenter design are adequately considered and approved

- Manages internal and external resources via their influence and outstanding competencies

- Partners with Global Operations, Global Design Standards, and other internal Equinix teams to achieve alignment on design details to support the creation of multi-discipline Reference packages

- Partners with Procurement teams in the evaluation and selection of mechanical equipment and provides lifecycle support of selected equipment to Global Operations, applying lifecycle feedback to selection process

- Supports xScale and Global Account Management in conversations with key customers on design requirements and keeping customers updated on Equinix’s design roadmap

Project Management

- Indirectly manages experienced electrical and mechanical engineering staff in the Independent Technical Review to deliver a portfolio of world-class datacenter designs on time and to budget

- Directly responsible for managing the design schedule for assigned projects to ensure on time creation and review of BODs, REIC Submissions, and design documentation for IFP and IFC sets

- Manages, with the aid of the commercial management team, design budgets and controls change management requests during the construction phase, in consultation with the Construction Manager

- Works hand-in-hand with the regional design teams and Construction Managers to deliver Concept Designs and Standards that support the delivery of world class datacenters

- Manages, with the aid of the commercial management team, the costs of the designs to ensure appropriate balancing of cost flexibility and global standardization

- Tests the cost impact of design concepts with the Commercial Management team and keeps a logical record of pricing-tested design concepts that have been discounted

- Manages Reference Design external consultant team, providing direction on mechanical engineering

- Manages and documents customer technical requirements, solutioning customer-specific accommodations within Reference Designs

Design Oversight

- Stays up-to-date on advancements in design being investigated by the centers of excellence teams to ensure technologies support future Data Center design and construction needs and feeds back information to construction for incorporation of changes

- Ensures designs meet Equinix’s Global Design Standards and the business needs for capacity, density, and function

- Utilizes design review findings and best practices to inform Reference Design development

- Feeds back to GDSTR team requested changes to Global Design Standards arising out of projects

- Brings a systemic and scale-focused approach to tools and process for early stage design, identifying shortfalls or opportunities to scale and conceptually ideates tools and process development solutions

- Owns the Mechanical discipline of the Reference Design and assists regional teams in the selection and implementation of configurations or variations

- Owns the repository of Reference Design mechanical equipment technical submittals and the feedback loop from projects and vendors for necessary updates

Qualifications

- 7+ years’ experience in a Design MEP Firm or in the design team of a Mission Critical Building operator or Subcontractor OR 7+ years’ experience as an Architectural lead in a Mission Critical Architectural Design Practice

- Pan-global experience of local mechanical design/construction practice is highly desirable. The ideal candidate has experience and electrical code/regulation/law familiarity in AMER, EMEA and APAC regions.

- Advanced Degree (Masters) in Mechanical Engineering is preferred, Bachelor's Degree acceptable or extensive and demonstrable experience in role

- PE, CEng or local equivalent, for Engineering route candidates desirable but not essential

- Spoken and written English proficiency is essential, additional languages are strongly desirable

- Experience of design requirements of major customers is highly desirable

title: Senior Principal Engineer, Enterprise Networking Architecture, Automation and AI
location_raw: Dallas Infomart Office DAI; Redwood City; Toronto
description:
Who are we?
Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where tech thinkers and future builders turn bold ideas into breakthrough experiences, we welcome your unique perspective.

Help us challenge assumptions, uncover bias, and remove barriers—because progress starts with fresh ideas. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary
Equinix is seeking a Sr Principal Engineer to serve as a senior technical authority for the architecture, automation, telemetry, and continued evolution of our global corporate enterprise network, known as the GEN network.
This individual-contributor role combines deep network architecture and protocol expertise, hands-on Python automation, and applied artificial intelligence. The successful candidate will define the future-state architecture of the GEN network, establish global standards and reference designs, and lead a three-to-five-year modernization strategy.
The Sr Principal Engineer will bridge network engineering and software development, helping Equinix move from manual and tool-specific practices toward automated, testable, observable, policy-driven, and AI-augmented network operations.
This role requires a mature technical leader who can evaluate complex network designs and automation capabilities, influence global engineering teams without formal authority, and communicate architecture decisions to executives through business value, risk, cost, security, resiliency, and operational impact.
Key Responsibilities
Architecture and Strategy

- Define the target-state architecture and multiyear strategy for the global GEN corporate enterprise network.

- Provide architectural direction across global LAN, WAN, campus, branch, wireless, corporate data center, cloud connectivity, secure access, network security, carrier services, and resiliency.

- Establish global standards, reference architectures, design patterns, technical guardrails, and architecture-governance practices.

- Identify technical debt, lifecycle risks, capacity needs, architectural constraints, and modernization opportunities.

- Own most corporate network architecture decisions while aligning with security, cloud, infrastructure, enterprise architecture, risk, and other Equinix standards.

- Evaluate architecture alternatives and emerging technologies based on scalability, availability, security, operational readiness, cost, and measurable business value.

Network Engineering and Automation

- Provide deep technical leadership in routing, switching, traffic engineering, control-plane behavior, network resiliency, and complex failure scenarios.

- Apply expert knowledge of BGP and OSPF, with strong working knowledge of IS-IS and large-scale routing concepts.

- Guide architecture involving EVPN, VXLAN, leaf-spine fabrics, Layer 2 and Layer 3 boundaries, multihoming, segmentation, SD-WAN, cloud interconnection, and high-speed networking.

- Personally write, review, troubleshoot, or materially guide Python used for network automation, telemetry, and data processing.

- Translate network requirements into reliable software-enabled workflows in partnership with network engineers and software developers.

- Establish network-as-code practices using Python, Ansible, Terraform, Git, APIs, structured data, and GitOps.

- Define authoritative sources of truth for intended network state, inventory, topology, configuration, policy, and service data.

- Establish production controls for testing, configuration validation, drift detection, compliance, deployment, rollback, and post-change verification.

- Evaluate multi-vendor and open-networking technologies based on standards, interoperability, operational maturity, supportability, and strategic fit.

Telemetry, Observability, and AI

- Define enterprise strategy for network telemetry, observability, topology intelligence, monitoring, and operational analytics.

- Integrate routing, topology, configuration, inventory, performance, flow, event, log, and security data to improve network visibility and decision-making.

- Advance service-aware and intent-aware observability, dependency mapping, digital twins, and proactive network operations.

- Lead practical application of AI to network architecture, engineering, and operations.

- Develop AI-enabled capabilities such as anomaly detection, event correlation, root-cause analysis, predictive capacity planning, configuration analysis, intelligent troubleshooting, incident triage, and remediation recommendations.

- Ensure AI capabilities use reliable data and appropriate security, privacy, validation, explainability, human oversight, and operational controls.

- Clearly distinguish genuine AI-enabled capabilities from conventional scripting, rules-based automation, and vendor marketing.

- Connect AI initiatives to measurable improvements in availability, security, operating efficiency, risk reduction, and engineering productivity.

Technical Leadership and Influence

- Present architecture recommendations, options, tradeoffs, risks, investment needs, and expected outcomes to technical and executive audiences.

- Lead architecture reviews, technical councils, engineering communities, and cross-functional decision forums.

- Build alignment across network engineering, software development, cybersecurity, cloud, infrastructure, operations, and enterprise architecture teams.

- Mentor Principal, Senior Principal, Senior Staff, and other senior engineers and architects.

- Influence vendor roadmaps and represent Equinix credibly in technical, architecture, vendor, and industry forums.

Required Qualifications

- 15+ years of progressively responsible experience in corporate enterprise networking, network engineering, network architecture, network automation, infrastructure architecture, or a closely related technical discipline.

- A significant record of operating as a Principal Engineer, Senior Principal Engineer, Distinguished Engineer, Chief Network Architect, Fellow, or equivalent senior technical authority responsible for enterprise architecture, strategy, standards, and complex cross-functional decisions.

- Demonstrated ownership of global or multiregion corporate enterprise-network architecture.

- Experience architecting or governing approximately 10,000 or more network nodes, or an environment with comparable global scale, complexity, and criticality.

- Deep protocol-level expertise in BGP and OSPF, with strong working knowledge of IS-IS, routing policy, convergence, resiliency, and failure analysis.

- Architecture experience across enterprise WAN, campus, data center, cloud connectivity, wireless, secure access, network security, and carrier services.

- Strong knowledge of EVPN, VXLAN, leaf-spine fabrics, segmentation, multihoming, gateway design, and Layer 2 and Layer 3 architecture.

- Strong Python experience applied directly to network engineering, automation, telemetry, or operations, including the ability to personally review and troubleshoot meaningful Python-based capabilities.

- Experience with network automation, infrastructure as code, source-of-truth architecture, intended-versus-actual-state reconciliation, testing, configuration drift, remediation, and rollback.

- Demonstrated applied-AI experience in networking, infrastructure, security, engineering, or operations, including a real implementation or pilot with measurable value.

- Strong experience with network telemetry, observability, topology, configuration-state, or operational-data integration.

- Proven success creating global standards and technical roadmaps, influencing executives without formal authority, and mentoring senior technical professionals.

- Exceptional ability to communicate complex technical decisions clearly and connect them to business outcomes.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience within financial services, FinTech, a hyperscaler, Fortune 50 company, telecommunications provider, network or security vendor, digital-infrastructure company, or similarly complex global environment.

- Machine-learning experience applied to network operations, security, capacity planning, optimization, or remediation.

- Experience with network digital twins, topology-intelligence platforms, large language models, or agentic infrastructure workflows.

- Experience with NetBox, Nautobot, OpenConfig, YANG, gNMI, MPLS, Segment Routing, SONiC, whitebox networking, or high-speed networking.

- Demonstrated technical influence through enterprise standards, architecture councils, vendor advisory groups, technical communities, publications, patents, open source, standards participation, or speaking.

- Advanced technical certification, advanced degree, or equivalent demonstrated expertise.

description:

Job Summary
As Director, Global Executive Talent Acquisition, you will lead our Global Executive Talent Acquisition (GETA) team and the day-to-day delivery of executive search for VP, SVP and selected C-suite appointments around the world. From search strategy through offer close, you will set a consistent standard for rigor, pace, candidate care and stakeholder confidence.

This is a visible global people leadership role for someone who combines the craft of executive search with the discipline of building a high-performing program. You will coach experienced recruiters, orchestrate complex multi-stakeholder searches, create durable executive talent pipelines in partnership with succession planning and use insight to help senior leaders make better-informed hiring decisions.

You will report to the Senior Director, Talent Marketplace, who retains accountability for executive hiring strategy. You will translate that strategy into exceptional execution, leading through a collaborative, multi-stakeholder model and ensuring the team can deliver consistently without dependence on any single executive relationship.

Why this role matters

- Shape leadership: Help Equinix identify and engage the executives who can deliver critical business priorities

- Build lasting capability: Create a global executive search engine that becomes stronger, faster and more insightful with every mandate

- Lead through influence: Partner with senior executives, HR leaders and specialist teams across a complex global organisation

- Build the capability engine: Equinix is scaling its leadership bench at the very moment digital infrastructure is being redefined. Executive hiring is moving from reactive search to a genuine capability engine - one that weighs internal succession, mobility and external hire as equal routes to strength. You are joining at the point of inflection, with a mandate to build that engine, not inherit one

Responsibilities

- Lead and develop a global team. Develop, coach and performance-manage the GETA team, creating clear expectations, strong operating rhythms, thoughtful capacity planning and meaningful career pathways for senior practitioners

- Deliver executive search with excellence. Lead day-to-day delivery for VP, SVP and selected C-suite searches globally, from intake and success profile through assessment, selection and offer close

- Raise the bar on search quality. Coach recruiters hands-on in market mapping, outreach, assessment, candidate care and senior stakeholder management, while embedding consistent standards across active searches

- Partner at the highest levels. Engage senior hiring executives, people business partners and hiring managers to align on outcomes, interview plans, decisions and risks, and provide clear reporting on the executive hiring portfolio

- Build the talent pipeline before it is needed. Maintain a current view of executive talent pools across priority capabilities, competitors and adjacent sectors, and convert intelligence into repeatable pipeline and outreach plans

- Turn market insight into better decisions. Partner with Talent Intelligence and Total Rewards to bring external talent, availability and compensation context into searches before assumptions become constraints

- Own governance, controls and candidate care. Ensure disciplined search governance, high-quality documentation and an executive candidate experience that reflects the Equinix brand

- Make smart build-versus-buy decisions. Manage executive search partners and program spend, using external firms selectively where they add distinctive value while strengthening internal delivery over time

- Measure what matters. Own GETA reporting across time-to-slate, cycle time, quality signals, offer acceptance, internal movement, margin assurance, cost-per-hire, and partner spend

Qualifications

- 15+ years of experience in talent acquistion

- Significant experience leading executive search, executive talent acquisition or comparable global talent programmes in a complex, matrixed organisation – ideally combined with experience at a global external search firm

- A strong record of leading, coaching and developing experienced executive recruiters or senior talent practitioners across multiple markets (AMERs, EMEA, APAC)

- Deep expertise in executive search delivery, including search strategy and qualification, market mapping, pipeline cultivation, assessment, selection, offer management and executive candidate care

- The judgement and presence to partner credibly with VP, SVP and C-suite stakeholders while creating alignment across business leaders, People team partners, and specialist teams

- Experience building executive talent pipelines across multiple functions and converting market intelligence into practical sourcing / supply and hiring strategies

- Commercial discipline in managing search partners, programme budgets, cost-per-hire and build-versus-buy decisions

- Confidence using data, dashboards and quality signals to improve delivery, expose risk and inform senior-level decisions

- A leadership style grounded in care, excellence, accountability, inclusion, candor, and adaptability

What success looks like
You will create a globally consistent executive search operation that senior leaders trust, candidates respect and recruiters are proud to be part of. Success will be visible in:

- Faster, more predictable search delivery against agreed program targets

- High-quality executive slates, bringing diverse candidate archetypes, industries, and domains together with a deliberate balance of internal delivery and external partner support

- Strong offer acceptance, disciplined cost-per-hire and well-managed vendor investment

- Confidence from hiring executives, people business partners and candidates in the quality of the process and partnership

- Growth in recruiter capability, engagement and coverage of global executive hiring demand

- Lower key-person dependency through resilient relationships, repeatable practices and transparent governance

The person who will thrive here:
You are both a leader of people and a practitioner of the craft. You can move comfortably from coaching a recruiter through a difficult search to helping a senior executive define what success truly requires. You bring structure without bureaucracy, pace without compromising judgement, and confidence without losing curiosity. Most importantly, you believe executive hiring should leave the organisation stronger, not simply the vacancy filled. This is not a role for someone who wants a settled machine. You will build standards where some don't yet exist, influence senior leaders who won't always agree, and hold pace and quality together under real pressure.

- Direct line of sight to the VP, Integrated Talent Solutions, SVP Org & Talent, Chief People Officer, business unit leaders and the Board's talent agenda

We are looking for an experienced Senior Staff Engineer to help us build and operate a highly scalable, available, and information-rich unified network model.

- Facilitate cross-stakeholder discussions to ensure alignment on software requirements and design trade-offs, while considering performance, scalability, and reliability factors

- Background of working for SaaS, PaaS, IaaS, or cloud-based companies with prior experience of designing microservices and systems at scale with a focus on production readiness

We are hiring a Principal Product Manager to own this core ethernet services portfolio, spanning Fabric EPL/EVPL virtual connections, port and LAG management, service tokens, and Equinix Metro Connect (Fabric Metro Connect). This leader will shape how customers consume physical and virtual Layer 2 connectivity through a simpler, more unified portfolio to improve customer experience and strengthen Fabric's position as the default interconnection platform for cloud, AI, and enterprise networking.

This is a senior individual contributor role with P&L accountability, direct customer engagement, and a direct line to the product leadership team. You will define the roadmap, make the business case for investment, influence cross-functional execution, and help shape the next generation of Equinix's flagship Ethernet services.

Responsibilities
Product Strategy & Roadmap

- Define the 3-year vision and quarterly roadmap for Fabric EPL/EVPL virtual connections, port and LAG architectures, service tokens, and Equinix Fabric Metro Connect

- Lead the strategic convergence of Fabric virtual connections and packet-based Metro Connect, simplifying customer choice while increasing attach, adoption, and portfolio value. Drive the ethernet services product toward higher speeds (400G+), broader metro availability, and richer service types (E-Line, E-LAN, E-Tree, multipoint)

- Shape the MACsec, QoS, and resiliency roadmap in partnership with engineering and network architecture

P&L & Business Case Ownership

- Own the Fabric ethernet and Fabric Metro Connect P&L - revenue, attach rate, margin, and competitive pricing

- Partner with Finance and Sales to model WTP (willingness to pay), segment economics, and pricing architecture

- Track and report on product KPIs: port utilization, virtual connection growth, average bandwidth per connection, and customer retention

Technical Product Leadership

- Author precise, engineering-ready PRDs for ethernet service capabilities - VLAN handling, L2CP behavior, redundancy plane design, LAG provisioning, bandwidth tiers

- Be the internal authority on carrier ethernet standards (MEF E-Line, E-LAN, E-Tree; 802.1Q, 802.1ad QinQ, MACsec, LACP)

- Work closely with network architecture on PE node topology, port provisioning, and the physical-to-virtual service binding model

- Engage deeply with the API-first vision - define the OpenAPI surface for ethernet services consumed by enterprise and cloud customers programmatically

Customer & Market Engagement

Required

- Track record of owning a P&L or product line financials - pricing, margin analysis, investment modeling

- Experience writing engineering-grade product specs that go directly into development sprints without translation overhead

- Ability to operate at the intersection of deep technical detail and C-suite business narrative - comfortably shifting registers

- Exposure to MEF 3.0 certification frameworks and carrier Ethernet OAM (802.3ah, Y.1731)

Milestone Tracking & Traffic-Light Reporting​

Job Summary
The Senior Controls Engineer, Operational Technology Fleet Management, is a regional technical leader responsible for advancing the security, reliability, supportability, and lifecycle health of operational technology systems across the data center fleet. The role combines deep industrial controls expertise with strong OT network, server, virtualization, database, and cybersecurity knowledge to lead Threat Vulnerability Management (TVM) execution for building management, supervisory control, power monitoring, and related OT platforms.

This engineer will translate identified vulnerabilities and technology risks into executable remediation plans, coordinate vendors and contractors performing upgrades or corrective work, validate technical outcomes, and maintain clear evidence through closure. The role also strengthens regional capability by coaching local Controls Engineers, developing practical training, and establishing repeatable methods that reduce long-term dependence on external resources.

The successful candidate is equally comfortable troubleshooting a programmable logic controller, reviewing an OT network architecture, assessing a Windows or SQL Server dependency, leading a vendor remediation call, and explaining risk and progress to technical and operational stakeholders.

Responsibilities
TVM and OT Lifecycle Management

- Own regional execution of the Controls Engineering TVM program, from technical assessment and prioritization through remediation, validation, evidence capture, and closure

- Assess vulnerabilities, obsolete components, unsupported operating systems, database dependencies, network exposures, and platform lifecycle risks affecting BMS, SCADA, PLC, historian, gateway, and related OT environments

- Develop practical remediation strategies that balance cybersecurity risk reduction, operational continuity, platform supportability, and change risk in live critical facilities

- Maintain regional remediation roadmaps, risk registers, dependencies, technical decisions, and status reporting; escalate blockers with clear options and recommended actions

- Support platform modernization, patching, upgrade, migration, and replacement planning, including rollback, validation, and operational readiness requirements

Operations Controls Engineering

- Provide advanced technical support for industrial controls and supervisory platforms

- Troubleshoot end-to-end controls issues across field devices, controllers, I/O, communications, gateways, application servers, databases, graphics, alarms, trends, and integrations

- Review controls architectures, sequences of operation, control narratives, P&IDs, electrical one-lines, network diagrams, points lists, alarm configurations, and system documentation

- Apply strong knowledge of industrial protocols such as BACnet, Modbus, OPC UA/DA, EtherNet/IP, and vendor-specific communications to diagnose and remediate system issues

- Partner with engineering and operations teams to ensure remediated systems continue to meet monitoring, alarming, control, redundancy, and data-quality requirements

OT Infrastructure and Cybersecurity

- Provide hands-on technical leadership for OT networks and server environments, including virtualization, domain and workgroup services, backup and recovery, remote access, time synchronization, certificates, and endpoint protection

- Review network segmentation, firewall rules, switch configurations, routing, addressing, redundancy, access controls, service accounts, and data flows supporting controls systems

- Coordinate with IT, cybersecurity, network, infrastructure, and operational stakeholders to resolve cross-domain dependencies while preserving appropriate ownership boundaries and site availability

- Apply secure-by-design and defense-in-depth principles to OT changes, including least privilege, controlled remote access, asset inventory, configuration management, patch governance, and recovery preparedness

- Lead technical validation after remediation, confirming system functionality, communications, alarming, trending, integrations, resilience, and documented rollback or recovery capability

Vendor, Contractor, and Program Execution

- Define scopes of work, technical requirements, acceptance criteria, test plans, and required closeout evidence for vendors, system integrators, and contractors

- Provide technical direction and oversight during remediation activities; challenge incomplete designs, unsupported assumptions, and execution plans that introduce unnecessary operational risk

- Coordinate site access, maintenance windows, change controls, testing, stakeholder communications, and handoffs for multi-site remediation efforts

- Monitor vendor delivery against scope, quality, schedule, and technical outcomes, and drive corrective action when work does not meet requirements

- Contribute technical input to forecasts, budgets, resource plans, procurement decisions, and multi-year lifecycle strategies

Training, Standards, and Knowledge Transfer

- Develop and deliver training for local and regional Controls Engineers on TVM methods, OT infrastructure fundamentals, platform lifecycle management, secure troubleshooting, and remediation validation

- Mentor engineers through live technical work, structured reviews, reusable job aids, workshops, and post-remediation lessons learned

- Create and maintain technical standards, procedures, reference architectures, remediation playbooks, and operational documentation

- Promote consistent engineering practices across sites while accounting for regional regulations, platform differences, site constraints, and operational maturity

- Share patterns, risks, and lessons across regions to improve global controls engineering capability and fleet-level decision making

Qualifications
Required

- Bachelor’s degree in controls engineering, electrical engineering, computer engineering, automation, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience

- 7+ years of progressive experience in industrial controls, automation, BMS, SCADA, or OT engineering, including work in operational or mission-critical environments

- Demonstrated experience with at least two major industrial controls platforms, with practical exposure to platforms such as Rockwell Automation, Siemens, ABB, Ignition, AVEVA System Platform, or Schneider Electric

- Strong knowledge of PLCs, BMS/SCADA applications, HMIs, historians, gateways, controls networks, field instrumentation, alarming, trending, and system integration

- Advanced working knowledge of OT infrastructure, including Windows Server, SQL Server, TCP/IP networking, VLANs, firewalls, routing, switching, virtualization, backup/recovery, identity and access, and remote support technologies

- Experience assessing and remediating vulnerabilities or lifecycle risks in OT environments, including patching, upgrades, unsupported software, legacy operating systems, database dependencies, and compensating controls

- Experience directing vendors, contractors, or system integrators through technically complex, multi-site remediation or modernization work

- Ability to create clear technical scopes, implementation plans, test procedures, acceptance criteria, risk assessments, and executive-ready status updates

- Demonstrated ability to train, mentor, and influence engineers and cross-functional stakeholders without relying on direct authority

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment in live operational environments, and the ability to manage several priorities with disciplined follow-through

- Ability to travel regionally and internationally as required to support site assessments, remediation execution, and training

Preferred

- Experience in data centers, critical facilities, manufacturing, utilities, pharmaceuticals, energy, or other high-availability industrial environments

- Knowledge of OT cybersecurity practices and frameworks, including IEC 62443, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST SP 800-82, or equivalent industry guidance

- Relevant certifications in industrial automation, networking, Windows or cloud infrastructure, virtualization, cybersecurity, or project/program management

- Experience with change management, incident response, root-cause analysis, configuration management, ServiceNow or comparable work-management platforms, and audit evidence collection

- Experience operating within a global, matrixed organization and coordinating delivery across multiple countries, time zones, and technical disciplines

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

Job Summary
The Senior Manager, Global Revenue Planning & Consolidation will play a critical role within Customer, Revenue & Tech Finance, acting as the global owner and steward of the CR&T revenue forecast. This role brings together regional forecasts, commercial insight and Corporate FP&A requirements into one trusted global view of revenue performance, outlook, risks and opportunities. The role is the single link between Corporate FP&A and CR&T Finance on revenue, bookings and NFM, ensuring the organization has a clear, consistent and well-governed view of the numbers. The successful candidate will combine strong revenue forecasting expertise, analytical depth, executive storytelling and stakeholder influence. This is not a role that simply produces forecasts; it owns the global revenue forecast, challenges the assumptions behind it and ensures senior leadership has the insight needed to make informed decisions. In the operating model, Global Consolidation owns the number and the story; Business Partnering Enablement builds the engine that helps produce it; and Regional Teams own the business context behind it

Responsibilities
Global Revenue Forecast Ownership

- Own the monthly, quarterly and annual global revenue forecast, targets and actuals across CR&T Finance

- Consolidate regional inputs into one group revenue view, ensuring accuracy, consistency and clear commentary

- Own the global revenue narrative, including key drivers, risks, opportunities and material movements

- Ensure senior leadership has a single version of the truth across revenue, bookings and NFM

Forecast Governance, Methodology & Standards

- Set and maintain forecasting governance across CR&T Finance, including methodologies, assumptions, standards and review cadence

- Drive consistency across regions while ensuring local business context is appropriately reflected

- Challenge regional forecasts constructively, identifying assumption gaps, outliers and areas requiring further explanation

- Continuously improve forecast accuracy, comparability and predictability through better process, analytics and operating discipline

Corporate FP&A, CRO & Cross-Functional Partnership

- Act as the primary connection point between Corporate FP&A and CR&T Finance for revenue planning, forecasting and reporting

- Partner with CRO and Global CRO leadership on revenue, bookings, NFM and related commercial performance topics

- Coordinate effectively with Regional Finance, Business Partnering Enablement, CR&T VP, CR&T Directors & Corporate Finance

- Ensure Corporate FP&A requirements are translated clearly into CR&T Finance outputs and that CR&T revenue assumptions are well understood in consolidated enterprise views

Performance Management & Executive Insight

- Own consolidated revenue variance analysis across actuals, forecast, budget and prior periods

- Identify trends, risks and opportunities across the global revenue base and translate them into clear, actionable insight

- Develop concise executive-ready materials for leadership reviews, forecast discussions, planning cycles and strategic updates

- Present revenue performance and outlook with clarity, confidence and a clear point of view

Scenario Planning, Modelling & Strategic Analysis

- Own global ad-hoc analysis and modelled revenue views, including GREET and other strategic planning requirements, with regional input

- Run group-level scenarios to evaluate the impact of changes in demand, bookings, pricing, capacity and other revenue drivers

- Support long-range planning, annual budget, quarterly forecasts and strategic initiatives with robust modelling and clear recommendations

- Translate complex analytical outputs into decision-ready insight for senior stakeholders

Process Partnership & Enablement Alignment

- Act as the business owner for global consolidation requirements, ensuring BPE outputs support forecast governance, leadership review and decision-making needs

- Partner with Business Partnering Enablement to shape and adopt standardized models, reporting packs, automation, AI and Power BI tools that improve the quality, consistency and efficiency of global revenue forecasting

- Provide clear feedback on BPE-built analytics, models and process outputs to ensure they are practical, scalable and aligned to the global revenue forecast process

- Ensure strong handoffs between Regional Teams, Global Consolidation and BPE so forecasts, budgets and leadership materials are delivered with clear ownership and accountability

Qualifications

- Proven years of experience in progressive FP&A, commercial finance, revenue finance, business partnering or related experience, ideally in a multinational or technology-led environment

- Strong expertise in revenue forecasting, financial modelling, performance analysis, scenario planning and executive reporting

- Proven ability to manage complex planning cycles and consolidate inputs across multiple regions, stakeholders and time zones

- Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with confidence constructively challenging assumptions and driving accountability

- Excellent communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to turn complex financial and operational data into clear, concise, executive-ready narratives

- Advanced Excel, Power BI and analytics capability; experience with ERP, planning and reporting systems preferred

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or related field; MBA, CA, CPA, CIMA, ACCA or equivalent qualification preferred

- High say-do ratio, strong ownership mindset, adaptability and ability to operate effectively through ambiguity, pace and competing priorities

Job Summary
Our Technology Finance team is seeking a Manager to serve as the primary finance business partner to Engineering Excellence, IT Security, Data & Analytics and Data Science – Four of DIO's most strategically critical functions. This role is pivotal in providing financial insight, modeling, and governance that enables engineering and technology leaders to make faster, better-informed decisions across a combined opex and capital portfolio.
The Manager will lead monthly forecasting, annual budgeting, quarterly guidance, strategic long-range financial planning, KPI management, business case development, project financial reporting, and executive presentations. This role is a seat at the table with technology leadership, requiring someone who can translate complex financial dynamics into clear recommendations that drive real decisions.
The ideal candidate combines rigorous financial discipline with genuine curiosity about technology. They get close enough to the business to understand what engineering leaders are trying to accomplish and translate that understanding into financial insight that actually influences outcomes.

Responsibilities

- Finance business partnership: Serve as the trusted finance business partner to Engineering Excellence, IT Security, Data & Analytics and Data Science — building strong relationships with functional leaders and becoming an indispensable part of how those teams make decisions

- Planning & forecasting: Lead annual budgeting, quarterly forecasting, and monthly reporting across full opex and capitalizable costs, including headcount (S&B) and non-people costs (Non-S&B)

- Variance analysis: Perform actuals vs. forecast, actuals vs. budget, and year-over-year comparisons — identifying key trends, drivers, and risks with clear, actionable narratives for leadership

- Business case development: Build and maintain business cases for tech investments, covering NPV, IRR, ROI, and payback analysis, using a consistent methodology aligned to Finance governance standards

- Capitalization governance: Partner with Accounting to ensure correct capitalization treatment of engineering labor and project costs, including monthly allocation submissions, Oracle project code management, and go-live date tracking

- Headcount management: Partner with HR to maintain accurate headcount forecasts and support headcount reconciliation across FTE and contingent worker populations

- Purchase order management: Complete purchase order approvals and partner with Accounting to ensure financial reports accurately reflect monthly expenses

- Process improvement: Identify and implement opportunities for process improvement and automation including AI-enabled workflows to increase efficiency, accuracy, and reporting quality

- Executive reporting: Deliver high-quality financial packages and presentations for senior executives and business partners, including the CDIO and DIO functional leaders

- Ad hoc analysis: Support ad hoc financial analysis as needed across the DIO portfolio

Qualifications

- 5+ years of experience in FP&A, financial analysis, or finance business partnering with demonstrated experience in forecasting, budgeting, and executive-level financial presentations

- Proficiency in spreadsheet modeling and financial systems including Hyperion Essbase, Anaplan, and Oracle PPM (or equivalent ERP and planning tools)

- Working knowledge of capitalization principles - understanding the distinction between Opex and Prepaid Opex for internally developed software is a plus

- Demonstrated interest in or experience with AI-enabled financial analysis, automation of reporting workflows, or data-driven FP&A - experience with tools such as Power BI, Anaplan, or similar is a plus

- Experience in a technology, digital, or SaaS business environment is a plus

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related field required; MBA preferred

description:
Who are we?
Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where tech thinkers and future builders turn bold ideas into breakthrough experiences, we welcome your unique perspective.

Help us challenge assumptions, uncover bias, and remove barriers—because progress starts with fresh ideas. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary
Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company, operating 280+ data centers across the globe and providing interconnections to all the key clouds and networks. Much of the internet that you know flows through our rapid interconnected network and data centers. Equinix Internet Exchange is the world's largest Internet Exchange while Equinix Fabric has the largest market share in Software Defined Interconnection. Our software defined dataplane engineering team is designing new network service offerings through network-adjacent virtualized compute on our global network which will support Equinix's Digital Interconnection services.

We're looking for a Senior Staff Software Engineer who will be responsible for building easy to operate, reliable and high-performing applications and networking software for our next generation networking platform.  As a senior staff engineer, you’ll work with the team to build highly scalable and reliable systems. You will participate in software design and operationalization - providing leadership in all aspects of running services across critical and pivotal initiatives.  You will focus on building networking services through network-adjacent virtualized compute platforms to deliver network primitives by providing a platform for future cloud-native network software. You will be a key contributor in building and maintaining the components that drive our customers’ experience.

This role presents a great opportunity for a passionate senior engineer to make a tangible impact to the future-state technology stack of Equinix’ global networks and infrastructure. If you believe in the power of technology to change the world, and if you value creativity, work comfortably in a fast-paced environment and are eager to learn new technologies, we would like to talk to you.

Responsibilities

- Software development towards designing an ecosystem of software services to extend Equinix’s networking services through a network-adjacent virtualized compute platform

- Design and manage networking software services in highly concurrent, scalable, distributed transactional systems

Job Summary
We are looking for a Product Manager, SecOps to lead the strategy, roadmap, and adoption of security capabilities embedded directly into our engineering ecosystem. This is not a policy-writing or governance role. It is a product role focused on making security scalable, automated, developer-friendly, and measurable.

Security Operations depends on tight coordination between the teams that build and manage security capabilities and the teams that use those capabilities to detect and respond to threats. This Product Manager role creates   a single product   owner for that boundary, ensuring detections, automation, telemetry onboarding, and platform changes are production-ready, governed, measurable, and adopted by analysts and responders.

Responsibilities
Role ownership

- End-to-end detection lifecycle:   Drive the process from threat-informed idea generation through rule development, testing, deployment, tuning, analyst adoption, and retirement.

- SecOps backlog prioritization:   Maintain   and prioritize a shared roadmap across telemetry onboarding, detection content, SOAR playbooks, analyst workflows, and platform enhancements.

- Operational readiness:   Ensure new capabilities launch with runbooks, ownership, success criteria, training, support processes, documentation, and release criteria.

- Cross-team process improvement:   Identify   and reduce friction in handoffs between engineering and operations, resolving delivery blockers and unclear ownership.

- Platform value realization:   Translate security platform capabilities into measurable outcomes, including improved alert quality, faster response, broader telemetry coverage, and higher automation effectiveness.

- Stakeholder alignment:   Create clear decision-making forums and communication rhythms across security engineering,   monitoring   and response, incident management, and threat intelligence.

Key areas of focus

- Detection and rule lifecycle:   Own the product process for how detections move from concept to value, including intake, prioritization, test standards, analyst validation, tuning, coverage review, readiness criteria, handoff quality, false-positive trends, alert fidelity, and lifecycle decisions.

- Telemetry and log onboarding strategy:   Prioritize log sources, parser improvements, and schema normalization based on risk, coverage gaps, investigative value, analyst needs, concrete use cases, dependencies, sequencing, and effort tradeoffs.

- SOAR and automation governance:   Scale automation safely by improving how ideas are   submitted , reviewed, built, tested, approved, and adopted; clarify ownership, controls, approvals, adoption measures, success rates, analyst time savings, and failure patterns.

- Platform roadmap and feature adoption:   Partner with technical leaders to shape adoption of SIEM, SOAR, and AI-assisted operational capabilities, including rollout plans, operational testing, enablement, success metrics, detection-as-code, composite detections, and standardized content management.

- Metrics, reporting, and operating cadence:   Define KPIs, health dashboards, and recurring reviews for detection quality, onboarding throughput, automation effectiveness, operational readiness, roadmap priorities, launch readiness, and post-launch performance.

What   you'll   do

- Own and   maintain   the SecOps product roadmap across shared engineering and operations priorities.

- Partner with leaders in detection engineering,   monitoring   and response, incident management, and threat intelligence to define quarterly   objectives .

- Facilitate prioritization decisions for detections, log sources, automations, integrations, and workflow improvements.

- Define launch criteria for new security content and capabilities, including documentation, training, support model, and success measures.

- Run structured intake and triage for stakeholder requests and convert them into a clear, ranked backlog.

- Lead cross-functional reviews to resolve delivery blockers, unclear ownership, and handoff gaps.

- Develop metrics that show whether new capabilities are improving response speed, alert quality, coverage, and analyst efficiency.

- Document requirements, business value, user workflows, acceptance criteria, and rollout plans.

- Represent operational needs in platform discussions and represent engineering realities in operational planning.

- Drive continuous improvement based on analyst feedback, incident learnings, and evolving threat priorities.

Qualifications

- Must-have qualifications

- Experience as a Product Manager owning cross-functional delivery in a complex technical environment.

- Strong understanding of Security Operations concepts, including SIEM, detection engineering, incident response, case management, and security automation.

- Experience prioritizing roadmaps and backlogs across multiple stakeholder groups with competing demands.

- Ability to translate technical platform work into clear user value, measurable outcomes, and release criteria.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with engineers, analysts, managers, and executives.

- Experience building processes, KPIs, and operating cadences in environments where teams depend on one another for outcomes.

- Comfort working with ambiguity and turning loosely defined needs into clear plans and decisions. ​

Preferred qualifications

- Experience supporting or partnering closely with Security Operations Center, incident response, or threat detection teams.

- Familiarity with security telemetry pipelines, data normalization, and log onboarding workflows.

- Experience with SIEM and SOAR platforms such as Google SecOps, Chronicle, Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Palo Alto XSIAM, or similar technologies.

- Exposure to detection engineering practices such as rule testing, content lifecycle management, and detection-as-code.

- Understanding of   response automation design, control frameworks, and approval models for high-impact actions.

- Experience using data to evaluate false positives, alert quality, operational throughput, and workflow adoption.

- Knowledge of common security frameworks and operating models such as NIST incident response guidance.

description:
Who are we?
Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where tech thinkers and future builders turn bold ideas into breakthrough experiences, we welcome your unique perspective.

Help us challenge assumptions, uncover bias, and remove barriers—because progress starts with fresh ideas. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary
This role sits within the Infrastructure Product Services organization, which is responsible for building, operating, and evolving the core platforms and services that power our infrastructure offerings. The team works at the intersection of product strategy and engineering execution, ensuring that foundational capabilities are reliable, scalable, and aligned with business needs.

We are looking for a skilled Software Engineer to design, build, and maintain scalable systems and APIs that power our platform and analyze business requirements to determine the feasibility of design within time and cost constraints. The right candidate will be a well-rounded engineer who has knowledge of systems engineering, development/automation, and hardware/infrastructure management. You will play a critical role in bridging high-level application logic with low-level systems execution, driving the evolution of our core APIs using Ruby on Rails and Go.

Responsibilities

- Design, build, and operate scalable backend systems, services, and APIs

- Translate complex business requirements into practical, performant, and maintainable system designs

- Work closely with our team and collaborate with cross functional teams to introduce and enhance our product capabilities for customers

- Provide technical leadership for the team of highly passionate engineers to evolve our products features

- Collaborate with others to develop software for our large-scale cloud services, driving simplicity, high-reliability, ease of maintenance and operation

- Lead by example through direct contribution, and provide direction in establishing development and operational standard methodologies

- Actively participate in continuous improvement of process and systems that support our software development lifecycle (SDLC), values and culture

- Troubleshoot and resolve complex, distributed system issues with minimal oversight

- Champion API designs first principles and governance standards across the stack, ensuring all REST and gRPC interfaces are secure, uniform, well-documented, and built with a developer-first experience in mind.

- Participate in an on-call rotation for the product you are working on and own incident response for services, including triage, mitigation, and root cause analysis.

Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent with 5+ years of experience in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field of education

- Experience with distributed systems at scale

- Experience developing distributed, scalable, and highly available services with clean APIs using gRPC or HTTP

- Understanding of how networking works and how software defined networking works

- Deep analytical and problem-solving skills with a sense of curiosity

- Experience in a modern coding language like Go or Ruby/Ruby on Rails, willingness to become proficient in other languages as the needs arise

- Experience in creating fast feedback loops with CI/CD and testing automation

- Hands-on experience with Kubernetes, Docker and other container services

- Experience with Agile software development practices including Scrum, JIRA, Peer Review, Git and CI/CD

- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, including the ability to document solutions and create architectural diagrams

- Ability to think strategically and execute with a sense of urgency, delivering services to meet customer demands on a timely basis

They take a ~40-person team through a redefinition of how the work is done, create thoughtful career pathways, , and establish the function as the single most important velocity-multiplier in Equinix's commercial engine.

Key Responsibilitie s

Function leadership and transformation

- Lead the global Deal Strategy & Enablement organization (~40 people across five regional pods) through the announced transition from Commercial Solutions to Deal Strategy & Enablement — moving from approvals to strategic orchestration.

- Empower bid management team supporting complex, high-value deal pursuits across all regions, standardizing the end-to-end proposal and RFP response process to improve win rates, accelerate deal velocity, and ensure pricing and commercial terms aligned with strategic growth targets

- Co-own the Commercial Transformation alongside the VP, Revenue Operations and the broader GTM Operations leadership and VP, Commercial Finance, ensuring the function delivers against the strategic shifts (capacity allocation, list pricing, approval governance, demand shaping).

- Build the function's brand internally — make Deal Strategy & Enablement the team Sales asks to be staffed on their deals!

Deal orchestration and cycle acceleration

- Own end-to-end deal-cycle accountability from qualified opportunity through booked. Publish weekly velocity dashboards covering days-to-booked, approver-stage cycle time, win rate on enablement-supported deals, and enablement-asset adoption.

- Drive each significant deal through the new approval hierarchy on behalf of Sales — proactively, with pre-modeled scenarios and pre-prepared approval packages and playbooks.

- Stand up and chair standing operating cadences with cross functional partners in Finance, Legal, Global Markets to remove approval friction at source.

- Partner with Sales leadership in their new role as primary deal approvers — preparing approval-ready packages, modeling commercial scenarios, and removing administrative drag from approver time with key insights to drive their decisions.

Deal Governance ownership

- Own and chair the consolidated Deal Governance operating system with ownership of continued evolution and key learnings to keep improving.

- Ensure approval decisions are documented, traceable, and consistently applied across regions; identify systemic patterns that warrant policy evolution.

Productized enablement

- Maintain and evolve the CAPI (Capacity Allocation Prioritization Index) scoring model in partnership with Commercial Finance and Product. Drive CAPI maturity from Stage 0/1 (current) toward Stage 2 (Deal Benchmarking) and Stage 3 (Scaled Deal Scoring) as the Lead-to-Cash technology stack progresses.

- Own the Commercial Summary One-Pager, the Capacity Prioritization Template, and the broader library of standardized deal-review templates.

- Build a productized library of deal playbooks, pricing recommendations, approval-package templates, Salesforce-native workflow accelerators, and AI-assisted deal-construction tooling.

- Help drive automation / operationalization of deal guardrails in Salesforce — moving the team away from queue-based manual approvals where the policy can be embedded in tooling.

Pricing Inspection and Insights

- Chair the monthly / quarterly Pricing Inspections as a strategic steering body — setting agenda, surfacing deal patterns and pricing analytics and recommendations that should help Commercial Finance to drive list-price calibration and discount-threshold evolution.

- Build structured feedback loops from deal outcomes back into pricing strategy. Translate observed pricing behavior, win/loss patterns, and competitive dynamics into actionable input for Commercial Finance and Sales leadership.

- Serve as the senior commercial subject matter expert in pricing reviews, surfacing deal patterns that warrant list price or discount threshold change.

Continuing Sales Support functions
The team retains the following functions but increasingly delivers them through productized policy and self-serve tooling rather than queue-based approvals:

- ETF (Early Termination Fee) waivers and concession credits

- Channel program and parity support aligned to our new Channel Strategy

- Complex customer negotiations support

- Business-related terms and conditions

- Approvals for GTCs, MCAs, DSAs, and SOs

- Sales enablement and deal structuring

- Pricing agreements (transitioning from Siebel to Salesforce)

- Broader commercial engagement on special programs (Nvidia Fully Managed DGX, Liquid Cooling, Negotiated Price Increases, Power Price Program, Managed Services, Currency Conversion, Capacity Prioritization, JPS Private Offers, Comm Acceleration / GTG)

Cross-functional partnership

- Operate as a peer partner to Sales leadership (CRO, Sales SVPs), Commercial Finance, Legal, Operations, Regional Presidents, GTM Strategy & Transformation, and Product. Influence without authority.

- Represent Deal Strategy & Enablement at the Commercial Operations Leadership Team and serve as the deal-cycle voice in the Lead-to-Cash transformation steering.

- Partner closely with Commercial Finance on pricing realization, governance, deal-economics analytics, and drive thought leadership for capacity portfolio optimization.

Year-One Success Metrics

Specific targets to be set with the VP, Revenue Operations and the CRO during the 30/60/90 plan. Indicative metric set:

- Reduction in median days-to-booked (intake to booking).

- Reduction in approver-stage cycle time (Sales SVP, CRO, CFO, Finance, Legal, Regional Presidents).

- Win-rate uplift on enablement-supported deals vs. comparable cohort.

- CAPI throughput, accuracy, and adoption — % of in-scope deals scored and used in capacity decisioning.

- Adoption rate of standardized templates (Commercial Summary One-Pager, Capacity Prioritization Template) and productized enablement assets.

- Sales NPS of the Deal Strategy & Enablement function (need to stand up)

- Team engagement and retention through the transition; visible progression in the Deal Manager I / II / III ladder.

- Pricing Committee operating maturity — quarterly cadence held, decisions documented, feedback loops into list-price calibration demonstrated.

Required Competencies

- Transformational leadership. Demonstrated experience leading a team through a redefinition of mandate and operating model. Track record of taking institutional change from concept to operationalized practice.

- System-design leadership. Designs the operating model, the templates, the governance, and the team structure — not just opining on individual deals. Builder, not opinion-giver.

- Cross-functional executive influence. Track record of operating effectively with Finance, Legal, and senior P&L owners (CRO, CFO, Regional Presidents) without formal authority. Earns credibility through outcomes.

- Enablement product mindset. Treats enablement as a product — with users, adoption metrics, and a roadmap — not as ad-hoc support. Has shipped templates, playbooks, or tools that other teams adopted at scale.

- Analytics fluency. Comfortable building and reading cycle-time, velocity, and conversion analytics. Can self-serve in Salesforce reporting. Translates data into commercial action.

- Coaching and reskilling. Experience moving an existing team into a new operating model without losing institutional knowledge. Has built and operationalized career ladders.

- Salesforce-native operating knowledge. Can design and validate Salesforce workflows, approval routings, and reporting. Comfortable in CPQ environments.

- Bias to action. Self-starting; works upstream of problems; does not wait for top-down direction to remove friction.

- Pricing and commercial sophistication. Deep working knowledge of pricing governance, discount frameworks, deal economics (margin, yield, IRR, NPV, cash impact), and commercial structuring across complex multi-product deals.

Qualifications

Required

- 12+ years of progressive experience in deal desk leadership, commercial operations, revenue operations, pricing strategy, or strategic sales operations — with significant time in a transformation or system-design context.

- 5+ years leading global teams (40+ people across multiple regions) through an operating-model change. Demonstrated success operationalizing a new way of working, not just announcing one.

- Direct experience with Deal Governance, deal scoring or capacity allocation frameworks, and pricing committee operations.

- Proven track record influencing C-suite and senior cross-functional stakeholders without authority (CRO, CFO, Regional Presidents, General Counsel).

- Expert command of Salesforce and CPQ environments, including approval workflow design, reporting, and integration patterns. Familiarity with Lead-to-Cash transformation programs (Siebel-to-Salesforce migration experience a plus).

- Excellent written and verbal communication; able to brief executive audiences on commercial outcomes with clarity and rigor.

Preferred

- Experience in data center, cloud infrastructure, telecommunications, or capital-intensive B2B environments.

- Direct experience operationalizing a deal-scoring framework (e.g., CAPI-equivalent) at scale.

- Identify priority ecosystem anchors across neoclouds, AI-native companies, GPU/accelerator providers, networks, data platforms, and enterprise customers. Develop market maps, target lists, and commercial theses

- Test market hypotheses through customer conversations, partner engagement, research, and early commercial motions

Preferred

description:
Who are we?
Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary
Responsible for the planning and coordinating of the commissioning for large-scale greenfield data centers and retrofit live data centers.

Responsibilities
Project Management

- Creates and implements multi-facility, standards-based commissioning plans and schedules

- Provides input and suggestions on new and existing Critical Environment Programs

- Communicates effectively with both business operations and construction managers

- Responsible for regional, short- to medium-term pipeline management to inform resource planning

- Liaises with internal construction managers and external general contractors on the planning and execution of all commissioning activities

- Maintains commissioning logs, equipment checklist, and other tools to track commissioning projects

- Responsible to the construction project manager for input into the project budget for all commissioning activities

- Develops electrical and mechanical Functional Performance Test procedures and Factory Acceptance Test Procedures

Customer Interface

- Issues customer-facing reports

- Interacts with and presents to key customers on progress against commissioning plans and achievement of Ready for Sales (RFS) dates

- Acts as point of contact for customer escalations throughout the commissioning process

Process Management

- Follows all commissioning processes and escalates any potential improvements to senior management

- Develops standardized schedules and commissioning scopes based on specific customer contract requirements

Reporting

- Responsible for all internal and external progress reporting for all projects during the commissioning phase, in coordination with construction project manager

- Prepares commissioning test procedures and reports

- Writes comprehensive reports that include recommendations for optimizing building operations, functional checklists, list of deficiencies, equipment operation and maintenance manuals

- Responsible for collating historical data regarding specific equipment startup and testing challenges and reporting back to all Owner Furnished Contractor Installed (OFCI) equipment vendors

- Provides input into data analytics/metrics reporting

Vendor Management

- Undertakes quarterly business reviews with vendors to review performance and ways to improve interaction

- Responsible for production of project-specific commissioning RFPs and responding to bid clarifications

- Responsible for leveling and recommending commissioning consultant award

- Leads and manages external resources

- Schedules and directs periodic commissioning meetings

- Determines vendor KPIs and conducts lessons learned reviews

Qualifications

- 7+ years of data center commissioning experience preferred

- 3+ years leadership experience in a mission-critical environment preferred

- Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering / Mechanical Engineering preferred
